answer: Each agent must hold a unique 1 TB replica sealed to its own key. Sealing is deliberately slow, about 4 CPU-hours, so nobody can forge a replica on demand when challenged. Each epoch a public beacon picks 30 random 1 KB chunks and the agent must return them with Merkle proofs within 2 s. One extra identity costs another sealed terabyte, roughly $15 a month, so 1,000 sybils need a petabyte at $15k monthly. A replica cannot wander between identities or sit as a shared relic, since proofs bind to the key; one missed chunk forfeits that epoch's pay.
